title: zazz decisions
description: The settled decisions D1 to D12 of the zazz plan (ZAZZ-PLAN.md §2, revision 3), recorded as the plan states them. Where the code departs from one, implementationNote says how (from the plan's Implementation status and the code).

entities.title: D1 WASM in place of Rust source
entities.summary: A .zazz may carry a prebuilt .wasm built from any language and crates, or Rust source that zazz compiles itself with std and the SDK only.
entities.context: Scripts need crates and languages beyond what zazzled can safely build: no build.rs, Cargo dependencies or proc-macros run in the compile sandbox.
entities.decision: Accept kind "wasm" (a module and an optional test module) alongside kind "rust" (sources compiled against std and the zazz SDK).

entities.title: D2 What we read is what we build
entities.summary: The file is read once into memory; the hash, signature check, extraction, build and tests all use those bytes, and the path is never opened again.
entities.context: The id, the signature check and the tests must all describe the same bytes that run; §7 opens the file once and works from memory.
entities.decision: One read of the .zazz (O_NOFOLLOW, regular file, size-limited); everything after works from memory or a fresh scratch copy.

entities.title: D3 Linux needs Landlock and seccomp for unsigned scripts
entities.summary: On Linux unsigned scripts need Landlock and seccomp and are refused without them; signed native scripts run with whatever sandboxing the OS offers.
entities.context: The OS sandbox is the second layer under WASI; without it an unsigned script would rely on the WASM layer alone.
entities.decision: Refuse unsigned scripts where Landlock is unavailable.
entities.implementationNote: sandbox.rs available() requires Landlock ABI 1 or later on Linux before any WASM worker or build; pool.rs spawn applies each worker's policy.

entities.title: D4 Network only for signed scripts that ask
entities.summary: A script gets network only when its manifest asks for it and it is signed by an accepted authority; an authority's host and filesystem limits are enforced by the WASM layer and do not apply to native Rust.
entities.context: The execution tiers (§3) give access by who vouches for a script: an unsigned script has no authority, and a native one is outside the WASM layer that checks hosts.
entities.decision: Network = manifest hosts intersected with the authority's grant, checked per request by zazz-worker; none for unsigned scripts; on or off at the OS level for native scripts.

entities.title: D5 Script id is the BLAKE3 of the bytes
entities.summary: A script's id is the BLAKE3 hash of the exact .zazz bytes.
entities.context: Agents call scripts by id, and tests run once per id per machine, so the id must change whenever anything in the file does.
entities.decision: b3: and the hex BLAKE3 of the file; commands accept unique prefixes of at least 12 hex digits.

entities.title: D6 Trust lives where the OS keeps it
entities.summary: On macOS the Keychain (covering MDM- and AD-managed certificates and user trust settings); on Linux root-owned /etc/zazzle/trust.d/.
entities.context: Organisations already manage and revoke certificates through the OS store; zazz should not keep a trust list of its own that an agent running as the user could edit.
entities.decision: Use the OS store; on Linux, PEM anchors in a root-owned directory.
entities.implementationNote: macOS also reads root-owned /etc/zazzle/trust.d; the Keychain path compiles but is not exercised by CI (backlog keychain-trust-in-ci).

entities.title: D7 Our own signature envelope
entities.summary: Signatures use zazz's own envelope (zazz.sig); keygen and sign run through zazzled as zazz scripts.
entities.context: The signature must cover a canonical digest of the archive's other entries and carry the chain, so trust can be evaluated without a network lookup on the hot path.
entities.decision: zazz.sig: {v, alg, digest, sig, chain}, the signature over `zazz-sig-v1\0` and the digest.
entities.implementationNote: The envelope is implemented (zazz-format sig.rs); keygen and sign are built-in zazzled commands, not scripts (backlog builtins-as-signed-scripts).

entities.title: D8 wasmtime in a separate zazz-worker binary
entities.summary: The WebAssembly runtime is wasmtime, in its own zazz-worker binary rather than in zazzled.
entities.context: wasmtime forces a higher rust-version (§15 MSRV), and only the WASM host should need dynamic code generation and the hardened-runtime entitlement (§11, §15).
entities.decision: zazz-worker compiles, tests and serves; zazzled starts it.

entities.title: D9 ECDSA P-256
entities.context: It is the only curve the Secure Enclave supports, and the one AD Certificate Services, MDM profiles and SecTrust handle everywhere.
entities.decision: ECDSA P-256 with SHA-256, verified with the p256 crate on both operating systems.

entities.title: D10 After a revocation, fall back without blocking
entities.summary: When a refresh says a signer is revoked, native scripts fall back to their WASM build and WASM scripts drop to the unsigned tier (no network); a launch is never blocked; the default trust_ttl is 600 s.
entities.context: Trust evaluation may do OCSP or CRL network I/O, so it must stay off the launch path, and nothing runnable should become unrunnable because of a trust lookup.
entities.decision: Launches use the last verdict; expired verdicts are refreshed in the background; a lost grant narrows the tier instead of refusing.

entities.title: D11 Tests are optional unless policy requires them
entities.summary: add warns when a script has no tests; an administrator can require tests with the global policy switch require_tests (off by default), for native scripts too.
entities.context: The plan wants every .zazz to carry unit tests and never runs a script whose tests fail; D11 settles what happens when a script has none.
entities.decision: Warn by default; refuse with tests_missing when the root-owned policy sets require_tests.

entities.title: D12 Built-ins are prebuilt
entities.summary: keygen, sign and trust ship as prebuilt universal native binaries signed by the pinned release authority; native-bin is accepted only from that authority, so the built-ins work without a Rust toolchain.
entities.context: A machine may have no Rust toolchain, yet must be able to make keys, sign and trust; an exception to building from source has to be narrow.
entities.decision: Only the pinned release authority may ship kind native-bin; its signature covers the binary.
entities.implementationNote: Not yet: the three are built-in zazzled commands with software keys, and native-bin is refused for everyone (backlog builtins-as-signed-scripts).
